newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end at new highs after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end at new highs after rate cut.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 index set a new closing high on Friday after the Bank of Canada eased interest rates for the 11th time this year.
Analysts said the central bank's move was widely anticipated, but it provided enough momentum to push Canada's biggest stock market to its 54th record close of 1996.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 19.52 points to finish at 5758.75 in brisk turnover of 101.2 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.05 billion).
"It's a combination of the rate cuts and the market's strong performance over the last couple of months," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
Katzin said the TSE is enjoying an influx of foreign investment, lured by declining interest rates, low inflation and falling budget deficits.
Consumer products, gold and conglomerates led eight of Toronto's 14 sub-groups higher. The weak side included communications and financial services.
The Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25 percent, bringing the rate to its lowest point since December 1961.
The move prompted Canada's chartered banks to drop their prime rates to 4.75 percent.
Economists said rates may fall again if the Canadian dollar holds its recent gains and the economy remains weak.
* Spirits and entertainment giant Seagram Co. Ltd. jumped 1.15 to 51.25, powering a 175-point gain in the consumer products group.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. soared 2.40 to 23.60 on 3.6 million shares amid market rumors that the Indonesian government may grant work contracts for Bre-X's huge gold discovery.

* Bank shares were hit by profit taking after enjoying a strong run this week. Royal Bank of Canada fell 0.60 to 47.30 on 1.02 million shares, while Bank of Montreal dropped 0.45 to 44.05 on 731,000 shares.
* Inmet Mining Corp. topped the most active list, down 0.45 to 7.40 on 9.9 million shares.
